name: Glute bridge
movement: hips lifted to a line and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Phone on its side on the floor, side on to you, lying down with your knees bent and feet flat.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. I will wait while you get set up: lie down side on to it, knees bent.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone, knees bent, feet flat on the floor, arms by your sides.
words.top: Hips lifted until knees, hips and shoulders make one line, no higher, heels and toes down.
howto: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width, heels a hand from your hips.
Press through the heels and lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders make one line. No higher.
Squeeze at the top for the count, heels and toes down.
Lower slowly — the rep counts when the hips are back on the floor.
words.cannot: Whether the glutes or the lower back are doing the work: it sees the height and the line, not the muscle. If the back pinches, stop.
words.about: Glute bridge — lying on your back side on, knees bent, feet flat, phone on its side: the shin's angle at the heel between toe and knee, allowed 85–110°, which is where your feet are; the angle at the hip between knee and shoulder, at least 160° at the top; how far the hip rises above the knee, at most 3°; and the foot's line off the floor, ±10° — checked first, then the shin, then the hip. Hold two seconds at the top, lower slowly, and the rep counts when the hips are back down.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the lower back pinches. The lift comes from the glutes, not from arching the back.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold at the top.
words.harder: A weight across the hips; a longer hold; one leg at a time.
words.mistakes: Pushing the hips past the knees; heels lifting; feet too far out.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee
measurements.why: Where the feet are: over the band the knee leans toward the head (feet too far out), under it the knee is out over the toes (feet too close). Not judged while a heel or toe is off the floor.

measurements.label: knee, hip, shoulder

settings.label: Hip angle at the top, at least

measurements.why: The top of the rep: straight is 180, and the line is asked for to within twenty degrees. Also the progress measurement: the lift is called at raiseAt, the return at downAt.

measurements.label: hip above knee

settings.label: Hip above the knee, at most

measurements.why: The rise of the knee-to-hip line: level is 0. The hips are not to go higher than the knees; the three degrees are for the pose model's wobble.

measurements.label: foot off the floor

settings.label: Foot off the floor, at most

measurements.why: The foot line, heel against toe: heels lifting tilt it one way, toes lifting the other. Checked first, because the feet decide what the hips can do.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.deep: Heels down — they are coming off the floor

faults.label: Toes lifting
faults.deep: Toes down — they are coming off the floor

faults.label: Feet too far out
faults.deep: Walk your feet in toward you — they are well out

faults.label: Feet too close
faults.text: Walk your feet out a little
faults.deep: Walk your feet out — your knees are out over your toes

faults.label: Hips above knees
faults.text: Not so high — hips no higher than your knees
faults.deep: Lower your hips — they are well above your knees

faults.label: Hips short of the line
faults.deep: Higher — knees, hips and shoulders in one line

settings.label: Hip angle that counts as lifted
